title: Normalize request-signing headers and CORS behavior for OpenAI-compat layer
author: Priya Nair
commits: normalize: canonicalize incoming auth headers (Bearer, Project-Key, Org-Key) and prefer scoped token header
auth: add X-Redwood-Nonce header parsing and VerifySignedNonce helper
compat: openai-compat map Authorization->X-Redwood-Project-Key when present; preserve streaming proxy headers
cors: allowlist nonce/signature headers for preflight and expose them to browser clients
sdk: python + ts surface minor helpers and deprecation warnings for old header names
tests: add integration matrix for key types, streaming, and function-calling payloads
docs: update auth header semantics and migration guide
description: Motivation: customers integrating via OpenAI-compat and browser clients reported intermittent failures for streaming responses and function-calling when custom signing headers were rejected by CORS preflight or incorrectly normalized at the gateway. This PR standardizes header semantics across the gateway, openai-compat layer, SDKs, and docs. Changes include canonical parsing order for incoming credentials (scoped token header preferred, then project/org keys, then Authorization Bearer), an explicit X-Redwood-Nonce header with verification helper for request-signing workflows, and explicit preservation/passthrough of streaming-related headers so SSE/websocket style proxying and function-calling metadata are not dropped. We add CORS preflight allowlist entries for X-Redwood-Nonce, X-Redwood-Signature and X-Redwood-Signature-Alg and ensure those are included in Access-Control-Allow-Headers and Access-Control-Expose-Headers for browser clients. The OpenAI-compat mapping now translates incoming Authorization: Bearer <project_key> into an internal X-Redwood-Project-Key for downstream routing, while keeping compatibility with existing org-level keys; a deprecation header X-Redwood-Deprecated-AuthName is emitted when older header aliases are used. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is non-breaking for existing server-to-server integrations; browser clients using custom signing headers must include them in preflight or update to the new nonce header; migration guidance is in docs. Testing: added integration tests for streaming stability with both scoped tokens and project keys, function-calling websocket flows with signed nonces and replay protections, and CORS matrix across origins and credential types. Rollout: feature gated by config flag "auth.normalize_headers_v2" with safe default enabled; we will monitor header-related 4xx spikes and stream stability SLOs. Checklist: - [x] canonical header parsing implemented - [x] nonce verification helper + unit tests - [x] CORS preflight fixes - [x] openai-compat mapping updated - [x] SDK helpers and docs updated - [x] e2e tests added
changed_files: runtime/stream/proxy.go (passthrough for X-Redwood-* during SSE/Websocket proxying)
docs/openai/compatibility.md (compat notes, examples with function calling and streaming)

Author (Priya): Added micro-benchmark and results to PR description (no measurable latency increase, allocation impact <0.5%).

Author (Priya): Added metrics and console alert rule; also included a short FAQ in docs for common signing errors.

release_notes: Auth: canonicalized header semantics and added X-Redwood-Nonce for request-signing; browser clients must include nonce/signature headers in preflight or migrate to helper SDKs.
Compat: OpenAI-compat layer now preserves streaming headers and maps Authorization bearer project keys to internal project routing header.
Docs: migration guide and examples for signing + streaming added.
Instrumentation: nonce verification metrics and alerts added to detect misconfigurations.
Behavior: non-breaking for server-to-server integrations; feature is gated and enabled by default.
